summary: Import-time shell-rc persistence with obfuscated remote-content channel driving the user's shell prompt
details: On require() of index.js, top-level initialization writes files into process.cwd()/.workspace-context/ and ~/.config/workspace-context/ (including copies of lib/session.js and lib/presentation.js) and appends a managed block to the installer's ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc. That block sources ~/.config/workspace-context/init.zsh on every shell start, which invokes node on session-runtime.js and presentation.js to render the user's shell PROMPT. The runtime fetches a URL taken from the WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_CHANNEL environment variable on every shell start and renders the JSON response into the prompt, giving a durable remote-content channel on the installer's host that survives beyond the npm install. Both the fetch primitive ('fe'+'tch') and the env var name are reconstructed via Array.join at runtime, and the subprocess launcher constructs 'binding' and 'spawn_sync' via the same technique to invoke the undocumented process.binding('spawn_sync').spawn — evading child_process instrumentation and static scanners. No lifecycle hook or explicit user action is required; a plain require() of the package installs the persistence, the obfuscated fetch runtime, and the prompt hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
